findings.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — When no Integration row exists for the installation_id (webhook not yet processed, failed, or row deleted), the step calls next_step with no OAuth-user/sender check, so an attacker who OAuths as themselves and supplies a victim's sequential installation_id (racing the install webhook) still links the victim's GitHub installation to their Sentry org

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — Integrations created by this pipeline never get metadata["sender"] (build_integration only sets it from state["sender"], which is never bound; the pipeline binds github_authenticated_user), so after an org uninstalls (OrganizationIntegration deleted, Integration kept) any reinstall hits a KeyError 500; the test sidesteps this by also deleting the Integration

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — OAuth state is pipeline.signature, which is static and global (a hash of the view classes; the tests hardcode the same 9cae5e88... value for different users and orgs), so the state gives no CSRF protection: an attacker can make a victim's in-progress pipeline accept the attacker's OAuth code and bind github_authenticated_user=attacker

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:448 — request.GET installation_id overrides the value bound before OAuth, so installation_id is not tied to the OAuth-verified identity and can be swapped freely after authentication, which is what makes the DoesNotExist bypass exploitable

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — test_installation_not_found now passes on an OAuth state mismatch (state ddd023... vs pipeline signature) and the generic "Invalid installation request." message, so the 404 installation-not-found path is no longer exercised

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:454 — test_github_user_mismatch only asserts the generic error text, which is shared by the state-mismatch, missing-token, non-ACTIVE-integration and sender-mismatch branches, so it would still pass if the sender comparison were removed; there is also no positive test where the sender matches

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen (token exchange) and get_user_info run outside the try block, so a GitHub network or API error during the OAuth callback raises an unhandled 500 instead of the rendered failure dialog

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (500) for Integrations without a sender, since build_integration (line 376-377) only sets metadata["sender"] when the state has one, so integrations created through the pipeline or before this change never have it.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — When the Integration row doesn't exist yet (the webhook hasn't arrived or never came), the view calls next_step() without checking github_authenticated_user against the installer, so whether verification runs depends on a webhook-vs-redirect race and any GET-supplied installation_id is bound unverified.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — The OAuth `state` is pipeline.signature, a fixed per-provider value (tests hardcode the same 9cae5e88... for different users and orgs), not a per-session nonce, so the state check does not tie the callback code to the session that started it.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — The new status=ACTIVE re-lookup returns "Invalid installation request" for an existing but non-active Integration with no OrganizationIntegration, where the old code let that case proceed to next_step, and the error message is misleading.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — Only the response read/parse is inside the try, so network errors from safe_urlopen and HTTP errors from get_user_info (line 434) surface as 500s instead of the error() page.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:415 — OAuthLoginView hand-rolls the OAuth2 authorize/state/token-exchange/response-parsing flow ("similar to OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params/exchange_token") instead of reusing OAuth2LoginView/OAuth2CallbackView, creating a drifting second OAuth implementation in an integration module.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:393 — Integration module instantiates GitHubIdentityProvider directly and calls its OAuth client-id/secret/URL getters plus the module-level get_user_info, coupling the integration pipeline to identity-provider internals rather than a pipeline/identity boundary.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:141 — _(error_short)` applies gettext_lazy to a runtime variable, so the call-site literals ("GitHub installation pending deletion.", "Github installed on another Sentry organization.", "Invalid installation request.") are no longer extractable for translation, unlike the previous `_("...")` literals.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:129 — Module-level helper has the overly generic name `error` and untyped `request`/`org` params, making call sites (`return error(...)`) ambiguous and easy to confuse with logger.error or local `error` variables; a name like `render_installation_error` with typed params would be clearer.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:390 — OAuthLoginView.dispatch` leaves `pipeline` untyped while the sibling `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` annotates `pipeline: Pipeline`, weakening type checking across the new step.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — Authorize redirect URL is assembled by f-string concatenation without urlencode, so redirect_uri/state are not escaped and the query construction diverges from the urlencode pattern used elsewhere.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — Integration is fetched twice by the same external_id (line 478 inside the filter, then again here with status=ACTIVE), duplicating the lookup and making the two DoesNotExist branches behave differently (next_step vs error) for subtly different conditions.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:454 — installation_id is now bound to pipeline state in both OAuthLoginView (line 399) and GitHubInstallation, spreading ownership of that state key across two steps.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:393 — test_installation_not_found now fails on the state-signature mismatch ("Invalid installation request.") instead of the 404 path, so the IntegrationError "The GitHub installation could not be found." at integration.py:356 is no longer covered and the test name is misleading.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:235 — Tests hardcode the pipeline signature "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" in six places and index `responses.calls[2]`, coupling tests to pipeline signature generation and HTTP call ordering instead of reading the signature/state from the redirect.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (HTTP 500) for Integrations created through the Sentry pipeline, since build_integration only sets "sender" when state has one (line 376) and the tests confirm pipeline-created metadata has no sender. Reinstalling after a Sentry-side uninstall that leaves the Integration row in place will crash.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen for the OAuth token exchange is called outside the try block, so a GitHub timeout, connection error or DNS failure raises an unhandled exception (HTTP 500) in the user-facing install popup instead of rendering error().

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info is called without handling errors; it calls raise_for_status() and resp.json(), so a GitHub 401/403/5xx, rate limit or non-JSON body gives an unhandled HTTP 500 instead of the error page.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info makes its call to the GitHub /user API through a plain build_session() session.get with no explicit timeout, so a slow GitHub can hang the web worker during the install flow.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — The result depends on whether the installation webhook or the browser redirect arrives first. If the redirect wins, Integration.DoesNotExist skips the sender check entirely and build_integration saves an Integration with no "sender", which later hits the KeyError at line 503.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — The broad `except Exception: payload = {}` and every new error() return fail silently with no logging or metrics, so token-exchange, state-mismatch and user-mismatch failures all look the same ("Invalid installation request.") and can't be diagnosed.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — When no Integration row exists yet (webhook not yet delivered/failed), the pipeline skips the sender check and build_integration links any attacker-supplied installation_id via the App JWT, bypassing the new OAuth user verification.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — OAuth state is pipeline.signature, a static hash of the pipeline view classes (identical across users/orgs in tests), so it is not a per-session nonce and gives no CSRF/login-CSRF protection on the OAuth callback.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:448 — After OAuth, installation_id read from the GET query overrides the value bound before authorization, so the verified GitHub identity is not tied to the installation chosen at start and an attacker can swap in any id (exploitable together with the DoesNotExist bypass).

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — Sender check compares mutable, reusable GitHub login strings instead of the immutable user id, so a renamed/re-registered login could satisfy the check.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — Authorize URL is built by f-string concatenation without URL-encoding redirect_uri/state/client_id, which is fragile against parameter injection if any of these values contain reserved characters.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — No test covers the Integration-exists-without-OrganizationIntegration success path (sender matches) or an Integration whose metadata lacks "sender" (e.g. pipeline-created, as in test_basic_flow), which would raise KeyError/500

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — test_installation_not_found now fails on OAuth state mismatch ("ddd023..." != pipeline signature) so the 404 "installation could not be found" path is no longer exercised and the test passes for the wrong reason

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:454 — test_github_user_mismatch only asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." shared by every error() branch (bad state, missing token/login, inactive Integration), so it can pass without the sender check firing and has no matching-sender positive control

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — OAuthLoginView failure branches (state mismatch, unparseable token body, missing access_token at :431, missing login at :435) and the inactive-Integration DoesNotExist branch at :495 have no dedicated tests
tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:257 — Auth header check moved to hardcoded responses.calls[2], coupling the test to exact HTTP call ordering of the new OAuth steps

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:236 — Pipeline signature state "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" is hardcoded across ~7 call sites, breaking on any pipeline view rename and enshrining a deterministic (non-per-session) OAuth state
tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:423 — Hardcoded webhook HMAC signature ties test_github_user_mismatch to exact fixture bytes and webhook secret; should be computed in the test

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:117 — OAuth token-exchange and /user mocks never assert the posted code/client_id/client_secret or that the OAuth access token is sent to /user, so tests verify mocks rather than the exchange behavior

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — When no Integration row exists for the installation_id (webhook not yet processed, failed, or row deleted), the step calls next_step with no OAuth-user/sender check, so an attacker who OAuths as themselves and supplies a victim's sequential installation_id (racing the install webhook) still links the victim's GitHub installation to their Sentry org

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, when the provided `installation_id` does not correspond to an existing `Integration` row, the code catches `Integration.DoesNotExist` and immediately does `return pipeline.next_step()` (no further validation). The newly added OAuth identity check (`pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`) is only performed in the branch where an active `Integration` exists. Thus, for the “no Integration row yet” case, the pipeline can proceed without any OAuth-user/sender binding check, matching the finding’s claim of a bypass at that point in the flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:448 — request.GET installation_id overrides the value bound before OAuth, so installation_id is not tied to the OAuth-verified identity and can be swapped freely after authentication, which is what makes the DoesNotExist bypass exploitable

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the code sets `installation_id = request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))`, meaning a querystring `installation_id` will override the value previously bound into pipeline state in `OAuthLoginView` (`pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)`). Since the OAuth redirect back to Sentry does not carry `installation_id`, a client can supply an arbitrary `installation_id` on the post-OAuth request and it will be accepted and re-bound (`pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)`), breaking the intended coupling between the OAuth-verified user and the installation being processed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — test_installation_not_found now passes on an OAuth state mismatch (state ddd023... vs pipeline signature) and the generic "Invalid installation request." message, so the 404 installation-not-found path is no longer exercised

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OAuthLoginView` before `GitHubInstallation` in the pipeline. In `test_installation_not_found`, the new assertion is reached via the OAuth step where `if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature: return error(...)` returns the generic "Invalid installation request.". The test uses a mismatched state (`ddd023...` vs the earlier pipeline signature `9cae5e...`), so it never reaches the `GitHubInstallation` logic that would check the `installation_id` and potentially trigger an installation-not-found condition. This is a real, diff-grounded test coverage regression/misdirection, but not necessarily a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:454 — test_github_user_mismatch only asserts the generic error text, which is shared by the state-mismatch, missing-token, non-ACTIVE-integration and sender-mismatch branches, so it would still pass if the sender comparison were removed; there is also no positive test where the sender matches

adjudication.rationale: In the new flow, multiple distinct failure branches return the same `error()` response with the same generic text (e.g. in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`: state mismatch, missing access_token, missing user login; and in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`: `Integration.DoesNotExist`, non-ACTIVE integration, and the sender/login mismatch check). In `test_github_user_mismatch`, the assertions only check for the generic "Invalid installation request." content/template, so it doesn’t uniquely prove the sender/login comparison branch was the cause. Also, the diff adds a new sender/login match requirement (`pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`) but there is no explicit positive test covering the case where an existing ACTIVE integration has matching sender/login and the pipeline proceeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen (token exchange) and get_user_info run outside the try block, so a GitHub network or API error during the OAuth callback raises an unhandled 500 instead of the rendered failure dialog

adjudication.rationale: In the new `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the OAuth callback performs `req = safe_urlopen(...)` and later calls `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` without any surrounding error handling. Only decoding/parsing `safe_urlread(req)` is inside a `try/except`. If `safe_urlopen` (network/HTTP error) or `get_user_info` (GitHub API call) raises, the exception will bubble up and likely produce a 500 instead of returning the rendered failure dialog via `error(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — When the Integration row doesn't exist yet (the webhook hasn't arrived or never came), the view calls next_step() without checking github_authenticated_user against the installer, so whether verification runs depends on a webhook-vs-redirect race and any GET-supplied installation_id is bound unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `installation_id` is bound from `request.GET` (or prior pipeline state) via `pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)` before any verification. Then, if `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist`, the code immediately `return pipeline.next_step()` (without validating `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` against an installer identity). The new installer check only runs in the later branch where an ACTIVE `Integration` exists and compares against `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. This makes the intended verification dependent on whether the webhook (which populates `integration.metadata.sender`) has already created the Integration row, i.e., a webhook-vs-redirect race, and allows proceeding with an unverified GET-supplied `installation_id` in the `DoesNotExist` case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — The OAuth `state` is pipeline.signature, a fixed per-provider value (tests hardcode the same 9cae5e88... for different users and orgs), not a per-session nonce, so the state check does not tie the callback code to the session that started it.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the OAuth `state` value is set to `pipeline.signature` and the callback only validates `request.GET["state"] == pipeline.signature` (no per-request/per-session nonce is generated or stored). The tests assert a constant state value (`9cae5e88...`) across multiple flows/users/orgs, which supports that this `state` is not unique to the session initiating the OAuth request. That weakens the CSRF binding between the authorization code callback and the initiating browser session.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — The new status=ACTIVE re-lookup returns "Invalid installation request" for an existing but non-active Integration with no OrganizationIntegration, where the old code let that case proceed to next_step, and the error message is misleading.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior as described: previously, when `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` succeeded but `installations_exist` was false, the code would `pipeline.next_step()` (after binding `installation_id`). Now it re-fetches with `status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE` and returns `error(... ERR_INTEGRATION_INVALID_INSTALLATION_REQUEST ...)` if the Integration exists but is not ACTIVE (or if metadata checks fail). This is a concrete edge-case/behavior change and the generic “Invalid installation request” message could be misleading in that scenario, but the diff alone doesn’t establish that proceeding in the non-ACTIVE case is the correct/required behavior (it may be intentional hardening).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — Only the response read/parse is inside the try, so network errors from safe_urlopen and HTTP errors from get_user_info (line 434) surface as 500s instead of the error() page.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the call to `safe_urlopen(url=..., data=data)` is outside the `try` block, so connection/timeout/other network exceptions will propagate and likely return a 500 instead of rendering `error(...)`. Likewise `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is not wrapped, so exceptions from that HTTP call would also surface as 500s. The diff shows only the response body decode/`parse_qsl` is protected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:415 — OAuthLoginView hand-rolls the OAuth2 authorize/state/token-exchange/response-parsing flow ("similar to OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params/exchange_token") instead of reusing OAuth2LoginView/OAuth2CallbackView, creating a drifting second OAuth implementation in an integration module.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `OAuthLoginView` that manually implements an OAuth authorize redirect, `state` verification, token exchange via `safe_urlopen`, and response parsing via `parse_qsl` (see `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`: building the authorize URL, `if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature`, POST to `get_oauth_access_token_url()`, `payload = dict(parse_qsl(body))`). The code explicitly notes it is "similar to OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params/exchange_token" rather than reusing shared OAuth2 views/utilities. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/architecture concern (duplicated OAuth flow that can drift), but it is not inherently a functional defect based solely on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:393 — Integration module instantiates GitHubIdentityProvider directly and calls its OAuth client-id/secret/URL getters plus the module-level get_user_info, coupling the integration pipeline to identity-provider internals rather than a pipeline/identity boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` which directly instantiates `GitHubIdentityProvider()` and calls its OAuth configuration getters (`get_oauth_client_id()`, `get_oauth_client_secret()`, `get_oauth_authorize_url()`, `get_oauth_access_token_url()`) and also calls the module-level `get_user_info(...)` (added imports: `from sentry.identity.github import GitHubIdentityProvider, get_user_info`). This is a concrete coupling of the GitHub integration install pipeline to identity-provider internals, rather than interacting through a higher-level pipeline/identity abstraction. The finding is therefore valid as an architectural/scope concern introduced by this change, but it is not a verifiable correctness/security defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:141 — _(error_short)` applies gettext_lazy to a runtime variable, so the call-site literals ("GitHub installation pending deletion.", "Github installed on another Sentry organization.", "Invalid installation request.") are no longer extractable for translation, unlike the previous `_("...")` literals.

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `error()` wraps `error_short` as `_(error_short)` (added around line ~141). Call sites now pass plain string literals like `error_short="GitHub installation pending deletion."` and `error_short="Github installed on another Sentry organization."` without wrapping them in `_()`. Since extraction tools typically only pick up `_('literal')` patterns, these literals are no longer directly extractable from the call sites, unlike the previous inline `_("...")` usage shown in the removed code blocks. This is a real i18n/l10n regression risk, but it doesn’t break core runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:129 — Module-level helper has the overly generic name `error` and untyped `request`/`org` params, making call sites (`return error(...)`) ambiguous and easy to confuse with logger.error or local `error` variables; a name like `render_installation_error` with typed params would be clearer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a module-level helper `def error(request, org, ...)` with untyped params, and call sites like `return error(...)`. However, this is a naming/typing readability nit rather than a concrete, diff-verifiable correctness/security/behavior issue or a substantive architectural problem. No ambiguity or malfunction is demonstrated by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:390 — OAuthLoginView.dispatch` leaves `pipeline` untyped while the sibling `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` annotates `pipeline: Pipeline`, weakening type checking across the new step.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` is defined as `def dispatch(self, request: Request, pipeline) -> HttpResponse:` (no type annotation for `pipeline`), while the adjacent `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` uses `pipeline: Pipeline`. This inconsistency reduces static type checking clarity for the newly added pipeline step but does not indicate a runtime correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — Authorize redirect URL is assembled by f-string concatenation without urlencode, so redirect_uri/state are not escaped and the query construction diverges from the urlencode pattern used elsewhere.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the authorize URL is built via f-string: `...?client_id=...&state=...&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}` rather than using `urlencode`. While the current `state` (pipeline signature) and `redirect_uri` (from `absolute_uri(reverse(...))`) are unlikely to contain `&`/`=` and thus won’t obviously break, this is a diff-grounded robustness issue: it’s easy for future changes (or unexpected characters) to introduce malformed queries, and it diverges from the `urlencode(...)` pattern used elsewhere in the tests and codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — Integration is fetched twice by the same external_id (line 478 inside the filter, then again here with status=ACTIVE), duplicating the lookup and making the two DoesNotExist branches behave differently (next_step vs error) for subtly different conditions.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the integration is looked up twice for the same `installation_id`: first in `OrganizationIntegration.objects.filter(integration=Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)).exists()` (no status constraint) and later in `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)`. This both duplicates the DB lookup and makes the control flow differ depending on why the lookup fails: missing Integration in the first lookup leads to `pipeline.next_step()`, while a non-ACTIVE integration (or other DoesNotExist in the second lookup) leads to `error(...)`. That inconsistency/perf issue is real and grounded in the diff, but it’s not provably a correctness defect without additional context about intended behavior for non-ACTIVE integrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:454 — installation_id is now bound to pipeline state in both OAuthLoginView (line 399) and GitHubInstallation, spreading ownership of that state key across two steps.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", ...)` happening in two places: in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` when `installation_id` is present in `request.GET`, and again in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` after resolving it from either `request.GET` or `pipeline.fetch_state`. This isn’t a verifiable functional bug (it’s redundant but consistent), but it does spread responsibility for the same pipeline state key across two steps, which is an architectural/maintainability concern grounded in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:393 — test_installation_not_found now fails on the state-signature mismatch ("Invalid installation request.") instead of the 404 path, so the IntegrationError "The GitHub installation could not be found." at integration.py:356 is no longer covered and the test name is misleading.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `test_installation_not_found` no longer asserts the previous “The GitHub installation could not be found.” behavior. Instead it performs a callback GET with a deliberately mismatched `state` (`ddd...` vs the pipeline signature used elsewhere in the tests) and asserts `Invalid installation request.`—which corresponds to the new `OAuthLoginView` state check (`if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature: return error(...)`). This makes the test name misleading and drops coverage of the earlier “installation not found” error path (at minimum, the test no longer exercises/asserts that message).

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:235 — Tests hardcode the pipeline signature "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" in six places and index `responses.calls[2]`, coupling tests to pipeline signature generation and HTTP call ordering instead of reading the signature/state from the redirect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple tests asserting/constructing URLs with a hardcoded OAuth `state`/pipeline signature value `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` (e.g., `assert_setup_flow` asserts the full redirect query including that state, and other tests build `setup_path_2` using the same hardcoded state). It also changes an assertion to index `responses.calls[2]` instead of `[0]`, which couples the test to the precise ordering/number of HTTP calls introduced by the new `OAuthLoginView`. This is a real fragility/maintenance concern in the tests, but not a production correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (HTTP 500) for Integrations created through the Sentry pipeline, since build_integration only sets "sender" when state has one (line 376) and the tests confirm pipeline-created metadata has no sender. Reinstalling after a Sentry-side uninstall that leaves the Integration row in place will crash.
matched_golden_ids: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same root cause: accessing integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] without ensuring the "sender" key exists, leading to a KeyError for integrations created without sender metadata (e.g., pipeline-created).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen for the OAuth token exchange is called outside the try block, so a GitHub timeout, connection error or DNS failure raises an unhandled exception (HTTP 500) in the user-facing install popup instead of rendering error().

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the OAuth token exchange does `req = safe_urlopen(...)` before the `try:` block. Only `safe_urlread(req).decode(...)` and parsing are wrapped. If `safe_urlopen` raises (timeout/connection/DNS), the exception will propagate and likely return a 500 instead of rendering `error(...)`, affecting the user-facing install popup flow introduced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info is called without handling errors; it calls raise_for_status() and resp.json(), so a GitHub 401/403/5xx, rate limit or non-JSON body gives an unhandled HTTP 500 instead of the error page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new unguarded call to `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` (around the added block in `OAuthLoginView`), and unlike the preceding token parsing it is not wrapped in a `try/except`; only a missing `"login"` key is handled. However, the finding’s claim that `get_user_info` specifically calls `raise_for_status()` / `resp.json()` and will therefore throw on 401/5xx or non-JSON is not verifiable from this diff because `get_user_info`’s implementation is not shown. So the robustness concern is grounded, but the asserted failure mode isn’t directly confirmable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info makes its call to the GitHub /user API through a plain build_session() session.get with no explicit timeout, so a slow GitHub can hang the web worker during the install flow.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a call to `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, but it does not show how `get_user_info` is implemented (it’s imported from `sentry.identity.github`). Therefore the claim that it uses `build_session().get` with no explicit timeout cannot be verified from the PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — The result depends on whether the installation webhook or the browser redirect arrives first. If the redirect wins, Integration.DoesNotExist skips the sender check entirely and build_integration saves an Integration with no "sender", which later hits the KeyError at line 503.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that when `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist`, the code immediately `return pipeline.next_step()` and therefore does not perform the new sender/user comparison in that request. However, the finding’s core claim—that `build_integration` will create an `Integration` “with no sender” and that this will “later” deterministically trigger a `KeyError` at the `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` access—is not verifiable from this diff because neither `build_integration` nor the integration-creation metadata shape is shown here. The asserted webhook-vs-redirect race and resulting KeyError depend on unseen code/behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — The broad `except Exception: payload = {}` and every new error() return fail silently with no logging or metrics, so token-exchange, state-mismatch and user-mismatch failures all look the same ("Invalid installation request.") and can't be diagnosed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` with a broad `except Exception: payload = {}` around parsing the access-token response, and multiple failure paths (`state` mismatch, missing `access_token`, missing `login` from `get_user_info`, integration lookup failure, authenticated user mismatch) all return the shared `error()` helper without any logging/metrics in the shown code. As a result, several distinct failures surface as the same generic "Invalid installation request." response (unless explicitly overridden, as in pending deletion / exists on another org), which is a diagnosability/observability concern but not a clear correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — When no Integration row exists yet (webhook not yet delivered/failed), the pipeline skips the sender check and build_integration links any attacker-supplied installation_id via the App JWT, bypassing the new OAuth user verification.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, if the `Integration` does not exist (`except Integration.DoesNotExist:`), the code immediately `return pipeline.next_step()` without performing the new OAuth-bound user check (`pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` vs `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`). Since `installation_id` is still bound into pipeline state earlier (`pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)`), subsequent pipeline steps can proceed using an attacker-supplied `installation_id` even though the authenticity/user binding was only enforced in the branch where an `Integration` row already exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — OAuth state is pipeline.signature, a static hash of the pipeline view classes (identical across users/orgs in tests), so it is not a per-session nonce and gives no CSRF/login-CSRF protection on the OAuth callback.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the OAuth `state` parameter is set to `pipeline.signature` and validated by comparing `request.GET['state']` back to `pipeline.signature` (no other per-request/session nonce is generated or stored). The added tests also assert a fixed `state` value (`9cae5e...`) in the authorize redirect query, indicating this value is deterministic in the test setup rather than a per-login random nonce. If `pipeline.signature` is predictable/reusable across users or runs, the OAuth callback lacks proper CSRF/login-CSRF protection because an attacker could forge a callback with a known `state`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:448 — After OAuth, installation_id read from the GET query overrides the value bound before authorization, so the verified GitHub identity is not tied to the installation chosen at start and an attacker can swap in any id (exploitable together with the DoesNotExist bypass).

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `installation_id` is taken as `request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))`, so any `installation_id` provided on the post-OAuth callback URL will override the value previously bound into the pipeline by `OAuthLoginView` before redirecting to GitHub. The later identity-to-installation check (`github_authenticated_user` vs `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`) only runs in the branch where an ACTIVE `Integration` already exists; if `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, the code immediately `return pipeline.next_step()` without validating that the OAuth-authenticated user corresponds to the installer for that (now attacker-supplied) installation id. This matches the finding’s “override” and “DoesNotExist bypass” claims and is security-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — Sender check compares mutable, reusable GitHub login strings instead of the immutable user id, so a renamed/re-registered login could satisfy the check.

adjudication.rationale: The new authenticity check in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` compares `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` against `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` (a GitHub username string). That value is mutable (user can rename) and may be re-claimed by another account, so an attacker who later obtains the same login could satisfy the check despite being a different GitHub user. The diff shows no use of an immutable identifier (e.g., GitHub numeric user id) for this verification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — Authorize URL is built by f-string concatenation without URL-encoding redirect_uri/state/client_id, which is fragile against parameter injection if any of these values contain reserved characters.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the authorize redirect URL is constructed via f-string concatenation: `...authorize_url()?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}` without using `urlencode`. This is fragile if any of these values ever contain reserved characters (e.g., `&`, `?`, `#`), because it would break query construction and could enable parameter smuggling. However, from the diff the values appear to be server-derived/config-derived (`pipeline.signature`, `absolute_uri(reverse(...))`, and the configured client_id), so it’s not clearly an exploitable security bug based solely on the diff—more a robustness/hardening issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — No test covers the Integration-exists-without-OrganizationIntegration success path (sender matches) or an Integration whose metadata lacks "sender" (e.g. pipeline-created, as in test_basic_flow), which would raise KeyError/500

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the new authenticated-user check compares `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without guarding for missing keys. If an existing `Integration` record lacks `metadata.sender.login`, this will raise `KeyError` and produce a 500 rather than rendering the intended failure page. The diff provides no guarantee that `sender` is always present on `Integration.metadata` for this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — test_installation_not_found now fails on OAuth state mismatch ("ddd023..." != pipeline signature) so the 404 "installation could not be found" path is no longer exercised and the test passes for the wrong reason

adjudication.rationale: In `test_installation_not_found`, the second request uses a hardcoded OAuth `state` (`ddd023...`) that does not match the pipeline signature checked in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` (`if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature: return error(...)`). That causes an early "Invalid installation request." error before any installation lookup/"installation could not be found" behavior can occur. So the test no longer exercises the original not-found path and can pass for the wrong reason.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:454 — test_github_user_mismatch only asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." shared by every error() branch (bad state, missing token/login, inactive Integration), so it can pass without the sender check firing and has no matching-sender positive control

adjudication.rationale: In `test_github_user_mismatch`, the assertions only check the shared failure template and the generic text `"Invalid installation request."`, which is returned by multiple `error()` branches in the new flow (`OAuthLoginView` bad state / missing token / missing user login, `GitHubInstallation` missing inactive Integration, and the new sender-login mismatch check). The test setup *likely* reaches the sender mismatch path, but the assertions do not uniquely validate that the specific `github_authenticated_user != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` check is what triggered the failure, nor is there a positive-control test for the matching-sender success path. This is a test coverage/robustness gap introduced by the change, not a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — OAuthLoginView failure branches (state mismatch, unparseable token body, missing access_token at :431, missing login at :435) and the inactive-Integration DoesNotExist branch at :495 have no dedicated tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds several new error branches in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` (token body parse failure -> `payload = {}`, missing `access_token`, and missing `login` from `get_user_info`) plus a new `Integration.objects.get(..., status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` failure path in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` that returns `error(...)`. The added tests cover the happy path and the GitHub-user-mismatch case, and `test_installation_not_found` now exercises the **state mismatch** branch (expects "Invalid installation request."). However, there are no tests in the shown diff that force (a) an unparseable token body, (b) a token response without `access_token`, (c) `/user` response missing `login`, or (d) an inactive/nonexistent ACTIVE Integration triggering the new `DoesNotExist` handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:257 — Auth header check moved to hardcoded responses.calls[2], coupling the test to exact HTTP call ordering of the new OAuth steps

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `auth_header = responses.calls[0]...` to `responses.calls[2]...` in `tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py` (around `assert_setup_flow`). The test now assumes the JWT-authenticated GitHub API request will always be the 3rd HTTP call, which is tightly coupled to the exact ordering/number of calls introduced by the new OAuth flow (`POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token`, `GET /user`, then later GitHub API calls). This is a real, diff-grounded test fragility concern, not a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:236 — Pipeline signature state "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" is hardcoded across ~7 call sites, breaking on any pipeline view rename and enshrining a deterministic (non-per-session) OAuth state

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple test call sites that hardcode the exact OAuth `state` value `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` (e.g. asserting the redirect query string and sending `state` in subsequent GETs). This is diff-grounded and makes the tests brittle: the value is derived from `pipeline.signature` in `OAuthLoginView`, so any change to how the pipeline signature is computed (including pipeline step ordering/renames) will break many tests. However, this is a test maintainability issue rather than a production defect. The claim that this "enshrines a deterministic (non-per-session) OAuth state" is not fully verifiable from the diff alone because `pipeline.signature`'s entropy/session binding is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:423 — Hardcoded webhook HMAC signature ties test_github_user_mismatch to exact fixture bytes and webhook secret; should be computed in the test

adjudication.rationale: In `test_github_user_mismatch`, the webhook POST sets `HTTP_X_HUB_SIGNATURE` to a hardcoded value (`sha1=d184e6...`) while the request body is generated from `INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE` and then mutated (`installation.id`, `sender.login`). This makes the test brittle to any change in the fixture JSON serialization/formatting or webhook secret/verification behavior; computing the HMAC from the actual `json.dumps(webhook_event)` bytes in the test would be more robust. This is a test maintainability concern, not a product defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:117 — OAuth token-exchange and /user mocks never assert the posted code/client_id/client_secret or that the OAuth access token is sent to /user, so tests verify mocks rather than the exchange behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new OAuth behavior in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`: it POSTs to `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` with `code`, `client_id`, and `client_secret`, then calls `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (which hits `/user`). In tests, `_stub_github()` stubs the token endpoint with a fixed body (`body=f"access_token={access_token}"`) and stubs `GET {base_url}/user` with `json={"login": "octocat"}`, but the tests never assert the POSTed parameters to the token endpoint nor that `/user` was called with the OAuth access token (e.g., Authorization header). Existing assertions (e.g. `responses.calls[2].request.headers["Authorization"] == "Bearer jwt_token_1"`) verify the later GitHub App JWT flow, not the OAuth exchange. So this is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage of the new logic, not a functional defect proven by the diff.
